title: PHANGS-ALMA: Arcsecond CO(2-1) Imaging of Nearby Star-forming Galaxies
question: How can we map CO(2-1) emission at cloud scales (~1 arcsec ~ 100 pc) across a representative sample of 90 nearby star-forming galaxies to measure the demographics, life-cycle, and physical state of giant molecular clouds and connect them to galaxy-scale properties?

data.arrays: 12-m main array, 7-m ACA, and 12-m total power (TP) single-dish antennas
data.angular_resolution: median 1.3 arcsec (0.6 to 2.1 arcsec) / 98 pc (26 to 183 pc) for 12m+7m+TP; ~7-8.7 arcsec for 7m+TP
data.sensitivity: median 6.2 mJy beam^-1 (85 mK) per 2.54 km s^-1 channel at native resolution; 50 mK at 150 pc resolution

recipe.goal: Assess sample selection accuracy and completeness via Monte Carlo simulation
recipe.method: Perturb catalog values of inclination, stellar mass, star formation rate, and distance for ~15,000 nearby galaxies over 10,000 realizations (with and without distance uncertainties) and check how many meet PHANGS-ALMA selection criteria.
key_parameters: Inclination uncertainty +-5 deg (capped at 90 deg); M_star uncertainty ~0.1 dex; SFR uncertainty ~0.15 dex; distance uncertainty 0.03, 0.06, or 0.125 dex
Selection criteria: -75 deg < delta < +25 deg, i < 75 deg, d < 17 Mpc, log10 M_star > 9.75, log10(SFR/M_star) > -11 yr^-1
assumptions: Catalog values from Leroy et al. (2019) and EDD represent the true underlying galaxy properties

recipe.goal: Estimate stellar masses and stellar mass surface density maps
recipe.method: Mask foreground stars and subtract background from S4G IRAC 3.6 um or WISE1 3.4 um images, interpolate masked pixels using radial median, convolve to 7.5 arcsec, and multiply by a radially varying mass-to-light ratio predicted from 15 arcsec radial profiles of SFR-to-WISE1 luminosity smoothed with a 2 kpc kernel.
key_parameters: Annulus for IRAC background: 1.5 to 3 r25; unmasked central region: 10 arcsec (IRAC) or 0.5 r25 (WISE); resolution: 7.5 arcsec for mass map, 15 arcsec and 2 kpc kernel for M/L profile; Equation 3 parameters: a = -11.0, b = -0.375, c = -10.2
assumptions: Chabrier (2003) IMF, Bruzual & Charlot (2003) models, and same mass-to-light ratio Upsilon_star^3.4 for 3.4 um and 3.6 um with inclination factor cos(i)

recipe.goal: Measure stellar disk sizes (effective radius Re and exponential scale length l_star)
recipe.method: Construct radial profiles of stellar mass surface density at 7.5 arcsec resolution (using mean within 30 arcsec and median within +-75 deg of major axis outside 30 arcsec), subtract background outside 2 r25, integrate out to 2 r25 to find half-mass radius Re, and fit an exponential over 0.4-1.0 r25 (adjusted by eye) to derive l_star.
key_parameters: Central aperture: 30 arcsec (all position angles, mean); outer rings: within +-75 deg of major axis (median); background: > 2 r25; integration limit: 2 r25; exponential fit range: 0.4 to 1.0 r25
assumptions: Azimuthal symmetry when integrating radial profiles

recipe.goal: Estimate integrated and resolved star formation rates (SFR)
recipe.method: Combine GALEX FUV (or NUV) and WISE4 22 um (or WISE3 12 um) luminosities using linear conversion factors C calibrated to the GSWLC.
key_parameters: log10 C: -43.42 (FUV), -43.24 (NUV), -42.73 (WISE4 with FUV), -42.79 (WISE4 with NUV), -42.63 (WISE4 alone)
assumptions: Recent star formation history does not vary strongly across the sample; Chabrier (2003) IMF via GSWLC calibration

recipe.goal: Process ALMA interferometric and total power observations into science-ready data cubes and moment maps
recipe.method: Apply ALMA pipeline calibration to 12-m and 7-m data; perform uv continuum subtraction, spectral regridding/rebinning to ~2.54 km s^-1, and empirical reweighting in CASA 5.6.1; run two-stage tclean (multiscale to 4 sigma, Hogbom to 1 sigma); apply primary beam correction and convolve to round Gaussian beam; linearly mosaic multi-part galaxies; feather with calibrated, baseline-subtracted TP cubes; convert to Kelvin; convolve to fixed angular and physical resolutions; generate 3D noise models, strict and broad masks, and moment maps (mom0, mom8, mom1, mom2, effective width) with uncertainty maps.
key_parameters: Multiscale clean threshold: 4 sigma; Hogbom clean threshold: 1 sigma; strict mask: S/N > 4 in 2 channels expanded to S/N > 2 in 2 channels; moment 1 prior tolerance: +-30 km s^-1 and S/N >= 2 in mom0; peak intensity boxcar kernel: 12.5 km s^-1; target resolutions: 2, 7.5, 11, 15 arcsec and 60, 90, 120, 150, 500, 750, 1000 pc (10% tolerance)
assumptions: Spatial and spectral variations of the noise in each cube are separable; conversion to molecular gas mass assumes Milky Way alpha_CO^(1-0) = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 and R_21 = 0.65 (giving alpha_CO^(2-1) = 6.7 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1) and fiducial line width 5 km s^-1 for sensitivity metrics

recipe.goal: Measure integrated CO(2-1) luminosities, derive WISE3 aperture corrections, and validate against IRAM 30-m HERACLES maps
recipe.method: Integrate 17 arcsec resolution PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) cubes within a wide mask to obtain L_CO; compute aperture correction as the ratio of total galaxy WISE3 flux to WISE3 flux within the ALMA footprint; compare integrated fluxes and pixel-by-pixel intensities at 17 arcsec resolution with IRAM 30-m HERACLES CO(2-1) maps for 18 galaxies.
key_parameters: Cube resolution for integration and HERACLES comparison: 17 arcsec; pixel-by-pixel comparison threshold: I_CO > 1 K km s^-1 (1,161 sightlines across 18 galaxies)
assumptions: CO(2-1) intensity tracks WISE3 12 um intensity linearly within individual galaxies

score_reason: All ALMA project codes, observation logs, target coordinates, distances, physical property tables, and calibration formulas are exhaustively tabulated, and both the science-ready data products and the CASA+Python processing pipeline are publicly released (with low-level pipeline parameters documented in the companion paper Leroy et al. 2021a).
rediscovery_reason: All raw ALMA data and high-level data products are public, the reduction pipeline is open-source, and the paper provides comprehensive quantitative benchmarks (integrated CO luminosities, cube noise/resolution statistics, WISE3 aperture corrections, and stellar mass/size measurements) for 90 galaxies.
